FOREWORD
This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. This standard supersedes the following Indian Standards: IS No. 3267 : 1981 3268 : 1981 3269 : 1981 3270 : 1966 Title General requirements of anchors (first revision) Specification for stockless anchors (for ship's use) (first revision) Specification for stock anchors (for ship's use) (first revision) Specification for stock and single fluke stock anchors (for harbour use)

The requirement of High Holding Anchors (HHP) has been included in this standard. While formulating this standard considerable assistance have been derived from JIS F 3301 : 2000 `Anchors'. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 15846 : 2010

Indian Standard ANCHORS -- SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE This standard specifies anchors for ship and harbour use (herein after referred to as `anchor'). 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties of agreements based on this standard are encourages to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No. 2985 : 1990 3261 : 1980 Title Steel castings for ship's structure -- Specification (third revision) Carbon steel forgings for shipbuilding industry (first revision) c) Stock anchor (Type A and B) (for ship and harbour use) (see Fig. 3,Table 4 and Table 5); and d) Single fluke stock anchor (Type A and B) (for harbour use) (see Fig. 4 and Table 6).

4.2 Normal Mass of Anchors The normal mass of anchors shall be as follows: a) Stockless anchors : Calculated gross mass. b) Stock anchors for ship use : Calculated mass excluding mass of stock. c) Anchors for harbour use : Calculated gross mass. 4.3 Actual Mass of Stockless Anchors Excluding Mass of Shank It should preferably be 3/5 of the actual mass of anchors, actual mass of stock of stock anchor, � of actual mass of anchor excluding shank and actual mass of stock of single fluke stock anchor, � of actual gross mass. 5 PERMISSIBLE DEVIATIONS 5.1 The dimensional tolerance on each part of anchor shall be � 4 percent and its maximum value shall be within �20 mm. The length of shank of stockless anchor, may be modified in an unavoidable case depending on the hawse pipe length. 5.2 The masses of individual anchors shall not vary by �7 percent of the tabular masses, provided that the total mass of the anchors is not less than that would have been required for anchors of equal masses. 5.3 The swing angles of stockless anchors, Type A, shall be within 39� to 42� and designated by the purchaser. Swing angles of stockless anchors, Type B, shall be 35�. The permissible tolerance of swing angles shall be �1�. The permissible difference between outboard and inboard swing angles of anchor fluke shall be determined between the parties concerned. 6 MATERIALS The material for each part of the anchor shall be as given in Table 7. 7 MANUFACTURING METHOD Cast steel shall be manufactured by casting in an electric furnace. Cast steel ingots shall be subjected to 1

3 CLASSIFICATION The anchors are classified according to their shapes as follows: a) Stockless anchor, Type A (for ship use); b) HHP stockless anchor, Type B (for ship use); c) Stock anchor, Type A (for ship and harbour use); d) Stock anchor, Type B (for ship and harbour use); e) Single fluke stock anchor, Type A (for harbour use); and f) Single fluke stock anchor, Type B (for harbour use).
NOTE -- Stockless anchors, Type B (for ship use) may be regarded as high holding power anchors defined by a classification society, if they are applied for type approval as high holding power anchors and approved as such. High holding power anchors, defined by a classification society shall have two time or more the holding power than that available with stockless, anchors, Type A (Stockless Buwer Anchor) of the same mass.

4 CONTRUCTION, SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 4.1 Construction, Shape and Dimensions of Anchors a) Stockless anchor, Type A (for ship use) (see Fig. 1 and Table 1 and Table 2); b) HHP stockless anchor, Type B (for ship use) (see Fig. 2 and Table 3);

IS 15846 : 2010 appropriate post-casting heat treatment according to wall thickness. 8 INSPECTION AND TESTING For anchors following inspections and testing shall be carried out: 8.1 Construction, Shape, Dimensions, Mass and Visual Inspection The construction, shape, dimensions, mass and appearance shall be inspected and shall comply with the requirements specified and shall also be free from detrimental defects to use. 8.2 Drop Test The test shall be performed on each steel casting of the anchor with the anchor head being hung vertically; the shank and stock horizontally; the body of stock anchor horizontally and vertically, and when they are respectively, dropped from 4 m height onto steel foundation, every casting shall be free from any crack or other defects. The steel foundation shall be so constructed that steel slab of 100 mm thick or more is laid over the top of concrete block of one meter thick or more. 8.3 Hammering Test After the drop test, the steel castings of the anchor shall be hung and hammered with a hammer weighing 3 to 7 kg, these shall be not result in any defects. 8.4 Proof Loading The stock anchor and single fluke anchor shall be subjected to proof inspection and no abnormal deformation or other defects shall be observed after the application of proof test load corresponding of the weighed mass of anchors as given in Table 8, onto the positions as shown in the following Fig. 5 on each fluke or stock anchor and single fluke stock, on both flukes simultaneously one side and next on the other side in turned over state for stockless anchor. When anchors are pulled form about 10 percent of proof test load to full load and when released to the initial. Load, the permissible change in the gauge length may be up to 20 mm (see Notes 1 and 2) (see also Fig. 5).
NOTES 1 Drop test, hammering test, and bending test shall be carried out for cast steel only. Also drop test shall be carried out for casings for anchors of ship use only. For anchors with a nominal mass of 0.18 or less. Drop test and bending test may be omitted. 2 The weighed mass of anchors shall be the one excluding the stock for stock anchor and single fluke stock anchor, and shall be the total weighed mass for stockless anchor.

9 DESIGNATION The anchors shall be designated by classification and nominal mass (for stock anchors, their applications shall be indicated). Example: Stock anchor Type A 1.500 (for ship use). 10 MARKING 10.1 The anchor shall be marked on its body with the following. 10.1.1 Stockless Anchor a) b) c) d) e) Weighed mass of anchor head, Total weighed mass, Manufacturer's name or mark, Proof test load, and Year and month of manufacturer or serial number.

10.1.2 Stock Anchor a) b) c) d) e) Weighed mass of stock, Weighed mass of body, Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, Proof test load, and Year and month of manufacture or serial number.

10.2 BIS Certification Marking The anchors may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 10.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to the manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: TED 17 (591).
